See also: croûton

English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
crouton
Wikipedia

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • croûton

Etymology

[edit]

Unadapted borrowing from French croûton.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Received Pronunciation) IPA(key): /ˈkɹuːtɒn/
  • (General American, dialects of Canada) IPA(key): /ˈkɹutɑn/, /kɹuˈtɑn/
    • Audio (US):(file)
  • (Canada, dialects of the US) IPA(key): /ˈkɹutɒn/
  • (General Australian) IPA(key): /ˈkɹʉːtɔn/
  • (New Zealand) IPA(key): /ˈkɹʉːtɒn/, [ˈkɹʉːtɔ̟n]
  • Rhymes: -uːtɒn

Noun

[edit]

crouton (plural croutons)

  1. A small, often seasoned, piece of dry or fried bread.
  2. (African-American Vernacular, slang) A Glock switch.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • water crouton

Translations

[edit]
small piece of bread
  • Dutch: crouton (nl) m
  • Estonian: krutoon, saiakuubik
  • Finnish: krutonki (fi), leipäkuutio
  • French: croûton (fr), crouton (fr)
  • Galician: carocho (gl) m, corrosco (gl) m, codela (gl) f
  • Georgian: ორცხობილა (orcxobila), კრუტონი (ḳruṭoni)
  • Icelandic: brauðteningur m
  • Italian: crostino (it) m
  • Polish: grzanka (pl) f
  • Russian: грено́к (ru) m (grenók), круто́н (ru) m (krutón)
  • Spanish: crutón (es) m (Southern Cone), picatoste (es) m, tostón (es) m
  • Swedish: krutong c
  • Turkish: kruton (tr)

[edit]
  • canapé

[edit]
  • contour, cornuto, countor
